name: Massachusetts
overview: Massachusetts provides a refundable senior circuit breaker for qualifying homeowners and renters and an income-tax deduction for qualifying rent. Locally administered property-tax exemptions are separate.

programs.name: Senior Circuit Breaker Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: At least one eligible taxpayer must be 65 or older by the end of the tax year.
programs.incomeDefinition: Massachusetts adjusted gross income with statutory additions and subtractions; excludes specified personal exemptions.
programs.incomeLimits: 2025 total income: $75,000 single, $94,000 head of household, $112,000 joint; married filing separately is ineligible.
programs.formulaSummary: Credit qualifying housing payments above 10% of program income, limited to the annual maximum. Owner expenses include property taxes after reductions and half of separately stated water/sewer charges. Renters use 25% of annual qualifying rent.
programs.application: File Schedule CB with the Massachusetts income-tax return; a return is required even when no tax would otherwise be due.
eligibilityNotes: 2025 assessed-value ceiling for homeowners is $1,298,000, before residential exemptions and after abatements.
Dependents, nonresidents, subsidized renters and tenants of tax-exempt property are excluded.
interactions: Subtract property-tax abatements, exemptions and other reductions when measuring owner payments.
programs.programYear: Tax year 2025; claimed with the return filed in 2026.

sources.title: 2025 tax tips for seniors and retirees

programs.name: Rental deduction
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested; deduct qualifying rent from Massachusetts Part B adjusted gross income.
programs.incomeLimits: No general income eligibility ceiling stated in the rental-deduction provision.
programs.maximumBenefit: Deduct up to $4,000; this is the deduction amount, not tax savings. Married filing separately: normally $2,000 each, with a consent-allocation exception subject to a $4,000 combined ceiling.
programs.formulaSummary: Deduct 50% of qualifying rent personally paid for a principal residence in Massachusetts, subject to the applicable limit. Each separately filing spouse remains limited to 50% of rent that spouse actually paid; consent may allocate more than $2,000 to one spouse within the $4,000 combined limit.
programs.application: 2025 Form 1: enter qualifying rent on line 14a and the deduction on line 14. Form 1-NR/PY uses lines 18a and 18. A separately filing spouse claiming more than $2,000 must attach the other spouse's signed consent statement.
eligibilityNotes: Rent must be paid to a landlord for the taxpayer's principal Massachusetts residence. Joint occupants claim only their own payments.
A third party paying rent while maintaining a principal residence elsewhere cannot generate the deduction for either party.

Exclude separately charged utilities, furnishings and parking, and exclude deposits or prepaid rent until applied as rent. Condominium association payments and tenant-stockholder payments to a cooperative corporation do not qualify.

Vacation homes, temporary-assignment lodging and student or faculty housing do not qualify when the taxpayer has a principal residence elsewhere. Hotel, motel or rooming-house occupancy requires a rental agreement.

Part-year residents use qualifying rent paid while Massachusetts residents. A nonresident's Massachusetts rental must be the sole principal residence, with no outside dwelling to which the taxpayer normally returns or could return in the future.
interactions: The consent statement for a married-filing-separately allocation must identify the consenting spouse's name, address, Social Security number and deduction amount.
This Massachusetts deduction does not apply to the federal return. It reduces taxable income rather than paying a rent rebate.
programs.programYear: Tax year 2025 rent; claimed on the Massachusetts return generally filed in 2026.

researchNotes: The legal household income definition differs from federal AGI.
Locally administered exemptions are context, not an additional statewide cash credit. The inventory does not enumerate every municipal option.

The rental deduction maps to the rent component inside ma_part_b_taxable_income_deductions, which combines several deductions. This mapping is not validated; its fixed MFS cap does not represent consent-based allocation, and qualifying-rent and residency rules require further model review.
